legs.label: CIN +2.5
legs.why: Pittsburgh ranks 31st in offensive EPA at -42.9 and converts just 20% of third downs, and Rodgers has not completed a pass over 20 air yards all season, which caps the Steelers' realistic ceiling against a Cincinnati defense that has not allowed a passing touchdown. That supports the Under strongly, and the total's move from 47.5 to 42.5 confirms the direction rather than contradicting it. The side is a thinner call: Cincinnati's edge is real, but the number has already run from -1.5 to -3.5, and laying points on the road into a Steelers defense that leads the league in defensive EPA with a league-high 13.7% sack rate is uncomfortable with Burrow nursing ribs after five sacks in Week 2. Pittsburgh +3.5 at home in a division game has legitimate merit, so the lean on the side is small and the Under is where the stronger case sits.

legs.label: Under 45.5 TEN@NYG
legs.why: The premise that Jaxson Dart starts does not hold — he is doubtful with a sprained MCL and Jameis Winston, who completed 40.7% of his throws in relief, is in line to start behind a line missing a questionable Andrew Thomas and without a fully healthy Malik Nabers. That is why a number that opened at Giants -5.5 to -6 is now -3 and already -2.5 in places, and the dog side is worth taking while the key number is still available. ESPN's own predictor has Tennessee at 59.6% against a market that makes New York a 57.2% de-vigged favourite, though Dimers sits firmly the other way, so confidence on the side stays low. The under is the firmer position: the total has dropped from 43 to 39.5 in two days, Tennessee is averaging 15.0 points and New York 17.0, and a backup quarterback in a 25%-precipitation, 17-mph-gust afternoon is not the setup for a shootout.

legs.label: Under 51.5 NE@JAX
legs.why: The projection lands almost exactly on the number, so the side is close to a coin flip and the lean is a small one toward the points. New England's defense ranks second in EPA per play, has allowed one offensive touchdown and is 0-for-3 in opponent red-zone touchdowns, which is the sturdiest thing either team has shown. The total is the cleaner read: New England is averaging 15.0 points on 32.1% third-down conversions with only two offensive touchdowns all year, both teams rank top-10 in time of possession, and the under is 2-0 in Patriots games. The counterweight is Jacksonville's 29th-ranked 6.1 yards per play allowed, which keeps confidence moderate rather than high.

legs.label: BUF -1
legs.why: Buffalo is 2-0 averaging 38.5 points and 7.1 yards per play while the Chargers sit 28th in points per drive and have scored exactly 14 in each loss. The personnel gap is concrete this week: Los Angeles has both starting tight ends on IR, its starting left guard and starting defensive tackle expected out, and Derwin James Jr. in a cast, all on a 10am body-clock road trip against a Bills team on extra rest that led the NFL with 14 pressures in Week 2 against an offensive line that put the ball on the ground six times. The total is the softer call: Buffalo has allowed 31 points in both games and 300.5 pass yards per game with no interceptions, which is enough to lift a bad Chargers offense, but 14 points per game is a real drag and models lean marginally under. I make it Bills by nine with the total landing just above the number.

legs.label: SF -2.5
legs.why: San Francisco is 2-0 with top-five scoring on both sides of the ball and a quarterback completing 80.4% of his throws, while Arizona just lost at home by 24 to Seattle for an eighth straight home defeat and ranks 24th in scoring. The concrete reason for the higher side confidence is the combination of that form gap and a series in which San Francisco's recent wins have repeatedly come by 16 or more, plus a look-ahead number of SF -11.5 that makes 8.5 a discount. The total is the softer read: my projection lands right around 46, since Arizona has no James Conner, has frozen out Marvin Harrison Jr., and faces a run-stuffing front, while San Francisco tends to shorten games once ahead. Models are genuinely split here — Dimers and Covers lean Under, CBS leans Over — so I am keeping that confidence low.

legs.label: CAR -2.5
legs.why: Carolina holds a clear efficiency and volume edge: 6.7 yards per play and 61 snaps a game against a Cleveland offence at 16.5 points, 52 snaps and the worst yards before contact in the NFL. That gap justifies laying a short road number even with Carolina's 28th-ranked defence and a patched offensive line. The total is the softer side: Cleveland's pace and red-zone problems argue under, but Carolina has hung 71 points in two weeks. A 24-20 projection sits just under the number, so the under is a lean rather than a conviction play.

legs.label: MIN -1.5
legs.why: Minnesota's defence is the clearest edge on the field: a league-best 33.6% pressure rate and the heaviest blitz rate in the NFL against a Baker Mayfield offence that has already taken seven sacks and produced three offensive touchdowns in two games. Tampa Bay is 0-2 and kicked four field goals in a home loss to Cleveland, which is the profile of a team that moves the ball and then stalls. The under is the softer of the two positions because Minnesota's own Week 1 game went 61 points and Kyler Murray's return could raise the Vikings' explosiveness, so it sits at a lower confidence. Getting Minnesota at only -1.5 on the road with the defence travelling better than the offence is the reason for a 3 on the side.

legs.label: NO -3
legs.why: New Orleans has out-gained its opponents by a wide margin (409 yards per game to Las Vegas' 300) and every public model lands on the Saints, from ESPN's FPI at 64.6% to SportsLine covering New Orleans in 57% of simulations. The Raiders' 13.5 points allowed per game was built against Miami and a depleted Chargers passing game, which is a meaningfully softer slate than the Superdome home opener. On the total, DraftKings' 44.5 is the highest number in the market with books as low as 42.5, and both Raiders games so far have landed on exactly 40 combined points. The counter-argument is real: New Orleans plays at the league's fastest pace and its Week 1 game produced 61 points, which is why this is a small lean rather than a strong one.

legs.label: LAR -2.5
legs.why: Denver is last in EPA allowed per carry and is giving up 157.5 rushing yards per game, while the Rams average 142.5 on a near-even Williams/Corum split, which is the cleanest structural edge in the game. The Broncos' own offense has converted 26.1 percent of third downs and only 42.9 percent of red-zone trips into touchdowns, and Bo Nix has thrown an interception in each of his two starts. On the total, all four games these teams have played in 2026 finished at 41 points or fewer, and the Rams defense is allowing 281 total yards and 16.5 points per game. The main things arguing the other way are altitude, a Sunday night home crowd and the fact that a Nacua absence would let Surtain II devote full attention to Adams, which is why I am not going higher than a 3 on either side.

legs.label: Under 47.5 NYJ@DET
legs.why: Detroit is the better team and should win, but the number is priced off Detroit's offence rather than the defence the Jets bring: New York is first in total defence at 197 yards a game, third in yards per play, and first in time-of-possession differential, which is how a favourite this size fails to cover. Detroit's own defence is genuinely bad, 917 yards and 71 points allowed with both starting safeties on reserve, so this should stay competitive rather than become a runaway. On the total, the Jets' pace and three-and-out rate cut the play count enough to project roughly 46 combined points.

legs.label: Under 46.5 KC@MIA
legs.why: Kansas City is clearly the better team, but 11.5 is a price rather than a projection and this specific Chiefs team converts yards into field goals — Harrison Butker kicked five of them in Week 2 on 523 yards of offense, and Kansas City is 2-8 against the spread over its last 10 games. A 1:00 PM ET kickoff in Miami Gardens in late September is a genuine fatigue variable for a visiting team, and Miami's only two offensive touchdowns this year have both been chunk plays, which is exactly the shape of a late backdoor cover. On the total, Miami has scored exactly 13 in both games and sits 1-for-5 in the red zone, so even a 30-point Chiefs afternoon leaves the number in reach of the under. Confidence on the total is held lower because Kansas City is averaging 32.0 points and one Miami garbage-time score puts this right on the number.

legs.label: Under 40.5 SEA@WSH
legs.why: Seattle's defense has allowed 17 points across two games and leads the league in yards per play allowed at 3.8, and it now faces a Commanders offense starting Marcus Mariota, who threw for 111 yards on 16 attempts in relief. Both Seattle games have stayed under and Washington's own scoring has come mostly in garbage time against Philadelphia and Dallas. The side is thinner than it looks: this line has travelled from Washington +1.5 to +7 purely on quarterback news, Washington is home for the first time this year, and Seattle's own offense is converting only 33 percent of third downs with a committee backfield. I project 24-16, which covers by a point and lands under the total, so the under is the stronger of the two positions.

legs.label: Ja'Marr Chase anytime TD
legs.why: Owns both Bengals receiving touchdowns this season and draws a secondary that ranks 31st in passing yards allowed and may again be without Joey Porter Jr.

legs.label: Chris Olave anytime TD
legs.why: Olave has 18 catches for 268 yards in two games as the clear alpha in the league's fastest-paced offense, and Las Vegas is thin at corner with Darien Porter's foot in question.
